fields.h1: Build a Spa Landing Page That Takes Every Request
fields.hero_description: Build a spa landing page with one treatment, its price, a short request form, and an email to the front desk for each request.
fields.features_heading: From the Treatment Line to the Front Desk
fields.features_subheading: A spa landing page sells one treatment and takes the request for it. Emergent builds each part below from your prompt.
fields.feature_1:
The treatment, its length, and its price

Name the treatment, how long it runs, and what it costs, and Emergent builds the page around it. Change the price by prompt, and the headline and the form show the new number.
fields.feature_2:
A short form, saved as rows

Every request lands as a row in a database you own, with the date the guest wants and each answer they gave. The front desk books from that table instead of a voicemail list.
fields.feature_3:
An email to the person who books it

When a request arrives, the app emails the person who books it, such as the front desk lead, with every answer in the message. A Slack alert to a manager works the same way.
fields.feature_4:
Spots left, counted as people book

The page counts bookings against the cap you set for each session and shows the spots left as they change. At the cap, the session shows Full and takes no more bookings.
fields.feature_5:
Your booking software, connected

Booking software with an API can sit behind the page, and the app sends each request into it and reads open times back. Name the tool in your prompt, and Emergent writes the link.
fields.feature_6:
Code on GitHub, or a page on your domain

On paid plans, export the page and its request table to your GitHub repository. Or keep it hosted on Emergent under your spa's domain; custom domains are included and use credits.

fields.usecase_heading: Spa Landing Page Examples by Type of Spa
fields.tab_content_1:
Firm for one guest, light for the other, in one request

Nettlebed Day Spa sells a 90-minute couples massage for $310. The form asks for a name, a phone number, a date, a time of day, and each guest's pressure: light, medium, or firm. Mara Kessington asked for Saturday afternoon, firm for her and light for Dev. Elowen Pratt at the front desk got the request by email.
fields.tab_content_2:
When checkout is within 24 hours, the request goes first

Hotel guests at Halcyon Cove Resort Spa request treatments from their phones. Each guest gives a name, a room number, a checkout date, and a treatment. A guest checking out within 24 hours is marked Before checkout and goes to the top of Juhani Esterly's list. Of today's 9 requests, 4 carry that mark.
fields.tab_content_3:
No more bookings once a session reaches 24 guests

Saturdays at Ironleaf Bathhouse run as 4 soaking sessions, each 2 hours long with room for 24 guests. Guests book with a name and an email, and the page shows the spots left as bookings come in. A session that reaches 24 is marked Full and closes. By Friday, 82 of the 96 Saturday spots were booked.
fields.tab_content_4:
Any headcount from 30 up goes to the events manager

Offices book Kiln Street Spa for chair massage days. Its corporate page asks for the company, the headcount, a preferred date, and a contact email. An inquiry for 30 or more employees reaches events manager Ruairi Dunmore as a Slack direct message. Pellham Freight asked for 45 employees on March 12.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Spa Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to a spa landing page that sells one treatment and gets every request answered, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one treatment the page sells
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Put the length and the price up top
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Ask only what the desk needs to book
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Show your own rooms and therapists
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose a single treatment or package, such as a 60-minute deep tissue massage, and the guest it suits. Link the page from the ad or post that names that treatment. Keep the full service menu on your website, one click away.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the treatment in the headline and give its minutes and price beside it. A line such as "60-minute deep tissue massage, $135" states both before anyone scrolls. Add one sentence on who performs it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the answers your front desk needs before it can confirm a visit, then cut every other field. Contact details and a preferred day are enough for a first request. Ask about preferences, such as pressure, only where they change the booking.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Use photos taken in your own treatment rooms and lounge, and name the therapists who work there. Leave stock photos of other spas out. Put the photos beside the price, not in a gallery at the bottom.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide who books from the page and who takes group inquiries. Route each request to that person by email or Slack, answers included. Set a call-back target, such as within 2 hours.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send a reminder the day before
fields.howto_step_6_des: Email each booked guest a reminder the day before the visit, with the arrival time, the address, and anything to bring, such as a swimsuit for the sauna. Add a line on how to reschedule. The app sends it from the booking row the desk confirmed.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Tag each ad link, then compare
fields.howto_step_7_des: Add utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign to every link that points at the page; Google Analytics says to use all three whenever you add parameters to a URL. Save the campaign on each request row, and compare requests by campaign at the end of each month.

faq_plan.q: What is a spa landing page?
faq_plan.a: A spa landing page is a single page that sells one spa treatment or package and asks the visitor to request it. It carries the price, the length, photos of the space, and a short form, with no full service menu or site navigation to wander into.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a spa landing page?
faq_plan.a: Pick one treatment, write down its length and price, and list the questions your front desk needs answered. Then describe the page to Emergent's AI landing page builder in a prompt. It builds the page and the request form, and keeps every request in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: What should a spa landing page include?
faq_plan.a: Put the treatment name, its length, and its price in the headline, then photos of your own rooms, a short request form, and one line on your cancellation policy. Add 2 or 3 reviews that mention the treatment by name. Leave out the full menu and the site navigation: the form should be the only next step.

faq_plan.q: Can a spa landing page use the same layout as a hair studio page?
faq_plan.a: Yes, the layout carries over: one service with its price, above a request form. The questions change. On a salon landing page, ask about the stylist and the service; on a spa page, ask about pressure or whether two guests book together.

faq_plan.q: How do I take appointment requests on a spa landing page without phone calls?
faq_plan.a: Put a short request form on the page and route each request to whoever confirms visits. On a page built with Emergent, every request lands in a database you own, and the app emails the front desk. Add a line under the form saying when a guest will hear back, such as the same afternoon.

faq_plan.q: Should a spa landing page list treatment prices?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for the treatment the page sells. Put the price and the length side by side in the headline, such as $135 for 60 minutes. If add-ons change the total, show the base price up top and list each add-on with its own price under it.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should the form on a spa landing page ask?
faq_plan.a: Limit it to what the desk needs to confirm: contact details, a preferred day, and one or two treatment questions. Cut any field the desk would not use on the first call. Apply the test you would on a mortgage landing page: ask for more detail after the first reply, not before it.

faq_plan.q: Can a spa landing page connect to my scheduling software?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the scheduling software has an API. Emergent builds the connection from your prompt, and each new request then appears in the calendar the front desk books from. Without an API, keep requests in the page's own table and book them by hand.

faq_plan.q: Can a spa landing page help fill quiet weekday appointments?
faq_plan.a: Yes, with an offer of its own. Build a second page for one weekday treatment, such as a Tuesday facial, and email it to past guests. Give it its own form. Its requests then stay separate from full-price bookings, and you can see whether the offer filled those hours.

faq_plan.q: Is a spa landing page enough without a full website?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the job is selling one treatment: a landing page takes visitors from one ad or email to one form. A website holds the full menu and the team. A business landing page can cover a single-location spa with a short menu. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing a page.
